attempt_deadline.description:
The deadline for job attempts. If the request handler does not respond by this deadline then the request is
cancelled and the attempt is marked as a DEADLINE_EXCEEDED failure. The failed attempt can be viewed in
execution logs. Cloud Scheduler will retry the job according to the RetryConfig.
The allowed duration for this deadline is:
* For HTTP targets, between 15 seconds and 30 minutes.
* For App Engine HTTP targets, between 15 seconds and 24 hours.
* **Note**: For PubSub targets, this field is ignored - setting it will introduce an unresolvable diff.
A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, terminated by 's'. Example: "3.5s"
attempt_deadline.rationale: Sets how long a job attempt may run before it is cancelled as DEADLINE_EXCEEDED. This is an operational timeout/performance setting and does not affect access, encryption, or exposure, so it is not a security policy target.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

description.description:
A human-readable description for the job.
This string must not contain more than 500 characters.
description.rationale: Only used to describe the purpose of the job thus does not have security related impact

name.rationale: Is not related to security practices as is only used for naming purposes

paused.description: Sets the job to a paused state. Jobs default to being enabled when this property is not set.
paused.rationale: Sets whether the job is paused or running. Whether a scheduled job is active is a team operational choice, not a security control; a platform policy cannot generically dictate that jobs be paused or running.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Used for the project idenfication but does not have direct effects on the security of the service

region.description: Region where the scheduler job resides. If it is not provided, Terraform will use the provider default.
region.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

schedule.description: Describes the schedule on which the job will be executed.
schedule.rationale: Only used to set the timer for the job which would not affect the data security

time_zone.description:
Specifies the time zone to be used in interpreting schedule.
The value of this field must be a time zone name from the tz database.
time_zone.rationale: Only used for schedule operational purposes thus does not have an effect on security principles

app_engine_http_target.description:
App Engine HTTP target.
If the job providers a App Engine HTTP target the cron will
send a request to the service instance

app_engine_http_target.body.description:
HTTP request body.
A request body is allowed only if the HTTP method is POST or PUT.
It will result in invalid argument error to set a body on a job with an incompatible HttpMethod.

A base64-encoded string.
app_engine_http_target.body.rationale: Only used in methods POST or PUT and is just HTTP data thus would not affect security aspects

app_engine_http_target.headers.description:
HTTP request headers.
This map contains the header field names and values.
Headers can be set when the job is created.
app_engine_http_target.headers.rationale: Only used to provide addtional context which has no effect on the security

app_engine_http_target.http_method.description: Which HTTP method to use for the request.
app_engine_http_target.http_method.rationale: Selects the HTTP verb (GET/POST/PUT/...) the job uses when invoking its own configured target. The verb is dictated by the target API contract, not a platform security concern, and no verb is inherently "malicious" for a self-configured request, so it is not a useful policy target.

app_engine_http_target.relative_uri.description:
The relative URI.
The relative URL must begin with "/" and must be a valid HTTP relative URL.
It can contain a path, query string arguments, and \# fragments.
If the relative URL is empty, then the root path "/" will be used.
No spaces are allowed, and the maximum length allowed is 2083 characters
app_engine_http_target.relative_uri.rationale: The relative path on the App Engine target the job calls. This is a team-defined path/reference to their own endpoint; there is no generic secure value to enforce, and "avoid sensitive data in the path" cannot be expressed as a structural platform policy.

app_engine_http_target.app_engine_routin.description: App Engine Routing setting for the job.

App instance.
By default, the job is sent to an instance which is available when the job is attempted.
app_engine_http_target.app_engine_routin.rationale: The available app instance which does not directly affect the security.

app_engine_http_target.app_engine_routin.description:
App service.
By default, the job is sent to the service which is the default service when the job is attempted.
app_engine_http_target.app_engine_routin.rationale: Names the App Engine service the job's request is routed to. This is a reference to a team-owned target service; we do not constrain which resource a job points at, and there is no generic secure value to enforce.

app_engine_http_target.app_engine_routin.description:
App version.
By default, the job is sent to the version which is the default version when the job is attempted.
app_engine_http_target.app_engine_routin.rationale: Only used to select version of service thus does not directly affect security

http_target.description:
HTTP target.
If the job providers a http_target the cron will
send a request to the targeted url

http_target.body.description:
HTTP request body.
A request body is allowed only if the HTTP method is POST, PUT, or PATCH.
It is an error to set body on a job with an incompatible HttpMethod.

A base64-encoded string.
http_target.body.rationale: The HTTP request payload sent by the job to its target. This is free-form, team-defined request content; there is no generic secure value to enforce, and it is treated the same as the App Engine target body (which is correctly false).

http_target.headers.description:
This map contains the header field names and values.
Repeated headers are not supported, but a header value can contain commas.
http_target.headers.rationale: Only used to provide addtional context which has no effect on the security

http_target.http_method.description: Which HTTP method to use for the request.
http_target.http_method.rationale: Selects the HTTP verb (GET/POST/PUT/...) the job uses when invoking its own configured target. The verb is dictated by the target API contract, not a platform security concern, and no verb is inherently "malicious" for a self-configured request, so it is not a useful policy target.

http_target.uri.description: The full URI path that the request will be sent to.
http_target.uri.rationale: Must use HTTPS in order to improve upon encryption

http_target.oauth_token.description:
Contains information needed for generating an OAuth token.
This type of authorization should be used when sending requests to a GCP endpoint.

http_target.oauth_token.scope.description:
OAuth scope to be used for generating OAuth access token. If not specified,
"https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" will be used.
http_target.oauth_token.scope.rationale: Defines the OAuth scopes granted to the access token the job uses to call Google APIs. A policy should require narrow, API-specific scopes to enforce least privilege; broad scopes (e.g. cloud-platform) over-grant what the job's token can do.

http_target.oauth_token.service_account_.description:
Service account email to be used for generating OAuth token.
The service account must be within the same project as the job.

http_target.oidc_token.description:
Contains information needed for generating an OpenID Connect token.
This type of authorization should be used when sending requests to third party endpoints or Cloud Run.

http_target.oidc_token.audience.description:
Audience to be used when generating OIDC token. If not specified,
the URI specified in target will be used.
http_target.oidc_token.audience.rationale: Will not provide addtional security as mismatched and misconfigured uri is automatically rejected thus making it more of a configuration

http_target.oidc_token.service_account_e.description:
Service account email to be used for generating OAuth token.
The service account must be within the same project as the job.

pubsub_target.description:
Pub/Sub target
If the job providers a Pub/Sub target the cron will publish
a message to the provided topic

pubsub_target.attributes.description:
Attributes for PubsubMessage.
Pubsub message must contain either non-empty data, or at least one attribute.
pubsub_target.attributes.rationale: The metadata of the pubsubmessage which does not have influence on securty aspects of the service

pubsub_target.data.description:
The message payload for PubsubMessage.
Pubsub message must contain either non-empty data, or at least one attribute.

 A base64-encoded string.
pubsub_target.data.rationale: Holds the data of the message but does not have direct impact on security attruibutes of the service

pubsub_target.topic_name.description:
The full resource name for the Cloud Pub/Sub topic to which
messages will be published when a job is delivered. ~>**NOTE:**
The topic name must be in the same format as required by PubSub's
PublishRequest.name, e.g. 'projects/my-project/topics/my-topic'.
pubsub_target.topic_name.rationale: Does not impact security as is only used as a naming convention

retry_config.description:
By default, if a job does not complete successfully,
meaning that an acknowledgement is not received from the handler,
then it will be retried with exponential backoff according to the settings

retry_config.max_backoff_duration.description:
The maximum amount of time to wait before retrying a job after it fails.
A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, terminated by 's'.
retry_config.max_backoff_duration.rationale: Only used to dictate the maximum backoff thus not a security related attribute

retry_config.max_doublings.description:
The time between retries will double maxDoublings times.
A job's retry interval starts at minBackoffDuration,
then doubles maxDoublings times, then increases linearly,
and finally retries retries at intervals of maxBackoffDuration up to retryCount times.
retry_config.max_doublings.rationale: Used to control the timer of max_doublings and has no impact on the securtiy of the service

retry_config.max_retry_duration.description:
The time limit for retrying a failed job, measured from time when an execution was first attempted.
If specified with retryCount, the job will be retried until both limits are reached.
A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, terminated by 's'.
retry_config.max_retry_duration.rationale: Used to dictate the maxiumum amount of retries thus not a security related attribute

retry_config.min_backoff_duration.description:
The minimum amount of time to wait before retrying a job after it fails.
A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, terminated by 's'.
retry_config.min_backoff_duration.rationale: Only used to dictate the minimum backoff thus not a security related attribute

retry_config.retry_count.description:
The number of attempts that the system will make to run a
job using the exponential backoff procedure described by maxDoublings.
Values greater than 5 and negative values are not allowed.
retry_config.retry_count.rationale: Number of times Cloud Scheduler retries a failed job attempt. This is a reliability/operational tuning value; capping retries does not improve confidentiality, integrity, or exposure, so it is not a platform security policy target.
